newsitem.title: USA: Rexene agrees to $600 million Huntsman bid.
newsitem.headline: Rexene agrees to $600 million Huntsman bid.

text.p: Rexene Corp., after rejecting three previous overtures, said Monday it accepted Huntsman Corp.'s fourth acquisition offer in a transaction valued at $600 million.

Under terms of the agreement, announced jointly by the chemical companies, Huntsman will pay $16 for each of Rexene's 19 million shares outstanding. It will also assume close to $300 million in Rexene debt.
Rexene said it cancelled a special shareholder meeting scheduled for June 12 and cancelled a share buyback tender.
Huntsman had made three prior offers to buy Rexene, which had said those offers were waged by press release and were not backed by cash.
Financing had been a major source of wrangling between the two companies, as well as between Rexene's board and a group of dissident shareholders who hold a 13 percent stake.
"That issue has now been resolved to the satisfaction of both parties," a Huntsman spokesman said.
Guy Wyser-Pratte, managing director of Wall Street arbitrage firm Wyser-Pratte & Co. Inc. and one of the dissident shareholders, said the deal was the most sensible outcome for all concerned.
"The company had been playing the Nancy Reagan 'Just say no' defence. We have now seen that the best answer is 'Just say yes' to your shareholders," he said.

Wyser-Pratte and another Wall Street firm, Spear, Leeds & Kellogg, control about 13 percent of Rexene shares and have frequently expressed frustration over the refusal of Rexene's board to allow Huntsman access to company records.
Huntsman said it had not talked to the dissidents during its final negotiations, which started on April 22, when Rexene allowed Huntsman access to its records.
Huntsman, based in Salt Lake City, is the largest privately held chemicals company in the United States, with annual sales of $4.3 billion.
Rexene, based in Dallas, has sales of $588 million. It manufactures products for the chemical and plastics industry.

"We have maintained our interest in Rexene because of the extraordinary synergies and efficiencies that would result from a merger of our two companies. We greatly respect (Rexene Chief Executive) Andy Smith and believe Rexene has built strong value in this business," said Huntsman Chief Executive Jon Huntsman.

A spokesman for Huntsman said that the two companies were discussing whether Smith would remain at the merged company. He declined to comment on whether Huntsman would have to raise capital to complete the deal, which is expected by the third quarter.
Rexene shares rose 62.5 cents to close at $15.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
